h1:
Bangkok Michelin Restaurants 2026
Fine Dining + Michelin Street Food
intro: Bangkok is a city where you can eat Michelin food for a few hundred baht or a few thousand. For 2026 the Michelin Guide Thailand lists around 30-plus starred restaurants in Bangkok, the country just gained its second three-star spot, and there's still genuine street food holding a Michelin star on the sidewalk. We've pulled together both ends: restaurants for a big-night-out and Michelin spots where a couple hundred baht still fills you up, with rough prices and real neighborhoods so you can actually plan.

blocks.html: Michelin in Bangkok lives in two worlds. The first is starred fine dining: book a month ahead, sit down to a dozen-plus courses, pay several thousand to low five figures per person, the kind of meal for a proposal, an anniversary, or celebrating something. The other world is Bib Gourmand spots and starred street food, where a couple hundred baht gets you fed. The 2026 Michelin Guide Thailand lists 137 Bib Gourmand restaurants across Bangkok and the surrounding area. We've mixed both into one list, ordered by occasion and budget.

Straight up: we haven't eaten at every single one. This list is drawn from the 2026 Michelin Guide Thailand and from real reviews by people who've been. Prices are rough figures as of early 2026 and shift with the menu and the season, so check the restaurant's page before you go.

blocks.text: Michelin-starred fine dining — for the big nights

blocks.html: These are the hard-to-book, big-ticket places, but they deliver a real experience. They're mostly tasting menus (set courses). Most ask for a credit card to hold the booking, and many charge a deposit if you cancel last-minute. If you're planning a proposal or an anniversary, book at least 3-4 weeks ahead.

items.name: Sorn (ศรณ์)
items.blurb: A three-Michelin-star southern Thai restaurant, only the second in the country to earn three stars. It serves traditional southern Thai cooking, elevated, across a long tasting menu of 20-plus courses using rare southern ingredients. It's the hardest table to get in Bangkok, booked out months in advance, so if you're going you need to plan for real.

items.name: Sühring
items.blurb: Modern German cooking from twin chefs Thomas and Mathias Sühring, bumped up to three Michelin stars for 2026. It sits in an old house with a garden in Sathorn, and the menu tells the story of homely German food through childhood memories. Warm and unstuffy.

items.name: Le Normandie by Anne-Sophie Pic
items.blurb: A classic French dining room on the upper floor of the Mandarin Oriental, right on the Chao Phraya River, raised to two Michelin stars for 2026 with chef Anne-Sophie Pic behind the menu. The river view at sunset is the draw, and it's about as romantic a setting for a proposal as you'll find. Smart-casual dress code.
items.meta: French · Chao Phraya riverside (Mandarin Oriental) · Tasting menu

items.name: Gaggan Anand
items.blurb: Chef Gaggan Anand's restaurant topped Asia's 50 Best in 2025. It's modern Indian food turned into full-on entertainment, a tasting menu of around 25 courses that plays with light, sound, and surprise service. It feels more like watching a show than eating dinner. Hard to book and one of the priciest tables in town.

items.name: Nusara
items.blurb: Thai food from Chef Ton (Thitid), built on his grandmother's recipes. A small, warm room in olive green and gold, with a view onto Wat Pho. It's intimate, personal Thai fine dining that's been on Asia's 50 Best for years. A good pick for a special meal when you want genuine Thai flavors.
items.meta: Contemporary Thai · Tha Tien (Wat Pho view) · Tasting menu

items.name: Potong
items.blurb: Set in the family's old shophouse in Chinatown (Yaowarat), serving Chef Pam's Thai-Chinese fusion built on a five-elements, five-senses concept across a 20-plus-course menu. The multi-storey old building has a hidden bar upstairs. Great for people who love a story and good design.

items.name: Le Du (ฤดู)
items.blurb: Another contemporary Thai spot from Chef Ton, focused on seasonal Thai ingredients, over in the Silom area. It's previously held the #1 spot on Asia's 50 Best. The menu is tighter than some of the others here, which makes it a good first dip into Thai fine dining.

items.name: Chim by Siam Wisdom
items.blurb: Old-recipe Thai cooking in a vintage wooden house in Sukhumvit, with the feel of dining in an old aristocratic Thai home. The menu revives hard-to-find traditional dishes, and it's easier on the wallet than a lot of this group. Good for bringing older relatives or for a Thai-style celebration.

Contemporary Thai in the Charoen Krung area, using 80% local Thai ingredients and 20% imported, which is where the name comes from. The menu is playful and willing to experiment, and the room is relaxed without being too formal. A good fit for a celebration when you want something contemporary but laid-back.
items.meta: Contemporary Thai · Charoen Krung · Tasting menu

blocks.title: How to actually get a table
blocks.html: Most starred restaurants book through their own site or a reservation platform (Hungry Hub, Chope), opening bookings about 1-2 months out. For a three-star like Sorn you basically have to watch for the day reservations open. If you're going for a birthday or anniversary, tell them when you book; a lot of places lay on a small surprise.

blocks.title: Want to taste deeper? Try a Bangkok food tour or cooking class
blocks.text: Half a day with a local who knows the lanes — or cooking a dish yourself — teaches you more than just eating. Book ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide.

blocks.text: Michelin street food — sidewalk stars, a few thousand baht and you're happy

blocks.html: Bangkok has a sidewalk stall that genuinely holds a Michelin star, Jay Fai, plus a whole stack of Bib Gourmand spots where you eat well for a few hundred to a couple thousand baht. No bookings needed (except Jay Fai, where the queue is real), but be ready for lines and hot, un-airconditioned seats, the trade-off for flavor that comes Michelin-backed.

items.name: Jay Fai (เจ๊ไฝ)
items.blurb: A street stall that's held a Michelin star since 2018 and still has it in 2026. Jay Fai, now 78 and famous for her ski goggles, stir-fries every dish herself over charcoal. The star of the show is her crab omelette, packed with chunks of crab meat. The price is steep for street food, but it's an experience. The queue is long, so go put your name down early or budget an hour-plus.
items.meta: Wok dishes/crab omelette · Maha Chai Road (near Democracy Monument)

items.name: Thipsamai Pad Thai Pratu Phi
items.blurb: Legendary pad thai in the Old Town, open for decades. The egg-wrapped pad thai and the shrimp-fat pad thai are the headliners, paired with fresh orange juice. It's a Bib Gourmand spot where tourists queue every night. Open evening to late.
items.meta: Pad thai · Pratu Phi (Old Town) · Open evening-late

items.name: Guay Jub Mr. Joe
items.blurb: Rolled rice-noodle guay jub in clear or thick broth, loaded with crispy pork and offal, in a peppery broth that hits the nose. A Bib Gourmand spot in Sathorn, very easy on the wallet, perfect for a warming evening bowl.
items.meta: Guay jub · Chan Road, Sathorn · Open evenings

items.name: Nai Ek Roll Noodles
items.blurb: An old-timer in Yaowarat, known for clear-broth rolled-noodle guay jub with the full set of pork bits and a deep, peppery broth. A Bib Gourmand spot that Chinatown locals actually eat at, open through to late. Great to drop into while you're grazing your way around Yaowarat.
items.meta: Guay jub/noodles · Yaowarat · Open late morning-late

items.name: Jok Prince
items.blurb: Charcoal-cooked pork congee in front of the old Prince cinema in Bang Rak. The faint smoky char off the charcoal is the charm. A Bib Gourmand spot open in the early hours and again in the evening, good for breakfast or a light late meal.
items.meta: Pork congee · Bang Rak · Open pre-dawn/evening

items.name: Prachak Roast Duck
items.blurb: A century-plus-old roast-duck shop in the Charoen Krung area. Roast duck and tender char siu pork with a rich gravy. A Bib Gourmand spot that's been a Bang Rak fixture for ages. Good for an easy lunch that's reliably delicious.
items.meta: Roast duck/noodles · Charoen Krung, Bang Rak

blocks.title: The truth about Michelin street food
blocks.html: Most of these places take cash only, the seating isn't air-conditioned, and the lines get long at peak hours, especially Jay Fai, where some days you wait an hour and a half. If you'd rather not risk it, go off-peak (late afternoon or just before closing) and bring enough cash.

blocks.text: How to pick the right place for the occasion

items: Proposal/anniversary + you want a view — Le Normandie on the Chao Phraya, or Nusara overlooking Wat Pho. Both are clearly romantic.
You want an exciting, show-like experience — Gaggan Anand, a long course that plays with light and sound. Great if you love surprises.
You want genuine Thai flavors without too heavy a bill — Chim by Siam Wisdom, Le Du, or 80/20, starting in the two-to-three-thousand-baht range.
You want to try Michelin on a tight budget — Bib Gourmand spots like Thipsamai, Guay Jub Mr. Joe, or Jok Prince, where a few hundred baht gets you Michelin-quality food.
You're chasing three stars — Sorn (southern Thai) and Sühring (modern German), both needing bookings weeks to a month ahead.

blocks.html: If you want to hit both fine dining and Michelin street food in one trip, here's a two-day plan paced so your stomach can keep up, with no two big meals colliding and sensible travel between them.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Old Town — Michelin street food + a special dinner

items.activity: Start the morning with Jok Prince in Bang Rak
items.note: Opens before dawn, still quiet, a warm bowl to start the day

items.activity: Go put your name down at Jay Fai early, in the Maha Chai area
items.note: The queue is long, so book your spot and wander the Old Town while you wait

items.activity: Head back for Jay Fai's crab omelette
items.note: Bring cash; it's a few thousand baht per person, but it's an experience

items.activity: Dinner at Nusara (Wat Pho view) or Potong in Yaowarat
Finish with Thipsamai pad thai at Pratu Phi (if you've still got room)
items.note: Something light, with fresh orange juice

items.activity: A light lunch at Guay Jub Mr. Joe, or Nai Ek in Yaowarat
items.note: A few hundred baht; save your appetite for dinner

items.activity: Rest at the hotel and get ready for the big dinner
items.note: Fine-dining spots usually have a dress code, check first

items.activity: Special dinner at Le Normandie on the Chao Phraya
items.note: Arrive a touch early to catch the sunset over the river

items.activity: Carry on to a riverside rooftop bar
items.note: Cap off a special evening with a city view

blocks.title: Pace your stomach
blocks.html: Don't book two fine-dining meals in one day. A dozen-plus courses really fills you up and sits heavy. Alternating a fancy meal with light street food makes the eating more fun and better value.

faq.q: How much do Bangkok Michelin restaurants cost?
faq.a: There are two groups. Most starred fine-dining spots are set tasting menus, starting around ฿2,500 and running into the low five figures per person (Sorn ~฿7,200, Le Normandie ~฿7,500, Gaggan ~฿9,000). The Bib Gourmand and street-food side, like Thipsamai or Guay Jub Mr. Joe, fills you up for a few hundred to a couple thousand baht.

faq.q: Is Jay Fai still open in 2026?
faq.a: Yes, it's still open and still holds its Michelin star in the 2026 Thailand guide. Jay Fai, now 78, still stir-fries herself over charcoal. The signature crab omelette runs around ฿1,000-1,800 per plate, with a per-person spend of roughly ฿1,500-3,000. Budget an hour-plus for the queue and bring cash.

faq.q: How far ahead do you need to book Bangkok Michelin-starred restaurants?
faq.a: Book the popular ones at least 3-4 weeks ahead. For a three-star like Sorn, tables fill months out, so watch for the day reservations open. Many take bookings through their own site or a platform like Hungry Hub and require a credit card to hold the table.

faq.q: How many three-star Michelin restaurants does Bangkok have?
faq.a: In the 2026 Michelin Guide Thailand, Bangkok has two three-star restaurants: Sorn (southern Thai) and Sühring (modern German), which just moved up to three stars and are the second restaurants in the country to reach that level.

faq.q: Where should I eat if I want to try Michelin on a small budget?
faq.a: Go for the Bib Gourmand and Michelin street-food spots, like Thipsamai pad thai, Guay Jub Mr. Joe, Nai Ek in Yaowarat, or Jok Prince. A few hundred to a couple thousand baht gets you Michelin-backed food with no advance booking needed.
